findings.title: Each has a non-substitutable place
findings.claim: At resurrection standing, aloneness can mark an irreducible place: everyone is included, yet no peer can occupy another person’s place.
findings.mechanism: Before-reading: “Alone describes who is or is not physically beside each arriver.” After-reading: “Alone marks an irreducible standing: no peer can occupy or absorb another person’s place.” The attributed HFT trace joins the exhaustive group, resurrection-standing scene, and fard’s one-without-counterpart core, changing aloneness into non-substitutable standing.
findings.reader_payoff: A crowd can share the event without one person replacing another; each presentation remains their own.
findings.containment: This is an attributed extension of local aloneness and judgment imagery, not a detailed account or ontology of the self.
